(basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 6,109 (8.0 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 3,055 (4.0 apg) }} '''Blake Austin Griffin''' (born March 16, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Griffin primarily played with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]], where he was named the [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|consensus national college player of the year]] as a sophomore. Griffin was selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the Clippers in the [[2009 NBA draft]], and was a six-time [[NBA All-Star]] and a five-time [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA]] selection. In January 2018, Griffin was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] and played for them until 2021. In March 2021, Griffin signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. In September 2022, Griffin signed with the [[Boston Celtics]], with whom he stayed until his retirement in 2023. Griffin won four high school state titles at [[Oklahoma Christian School]] under his father, head coach Tommy Griffin. Griffin played two seasons of college basketball for the Sooners before entering the 2009 NBA draft, when he was selected by the Clippers. During the final pre-season game of 2009, he broke his left kneecap, had surgery, and missed the entire [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]]. Griffin made his NBA debut as a rookie the [[2010–11 NBA season|following season]], in which he was selected as an [[List of NBA All-Stars|All-Star]], won the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]], and was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]]. Griffin was named to the All-NBA Second Team once again. ====New coach and owner (2013–2015)==== [[File:Blake Griffin Zach Randolph 20131118 Clippers v Grizzles.jpg|right|thumb|upright|Griffin and [[Zach Randolph]] of the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a 2013 game]] After a disappointing first round exit in the playoffs, the Los Angeles Clippers sought new leadership and hired head coach [[Doc Rivers]]. [[File:Blake Griffin dunk.jpg|right|thumb|140px|upright|Griffin hanging on the rim]] Standing at {{convert|6|ft|9|in|m}} and weighing {{convert|251|lb|abbr=on}}, Griffin played mostly as a [[power The dunks are great, but it's his multiple-layered impact that has paved his early road to stardom."
